problem: The rule omits the day-start snapshot exception and says every item reads the state left by smaller-numbered items.
correct: Extraction reads the open-question snapshot from the start of the item's day; it does not necessarily see questions opened by earlier items that day.
evidence: docs/DECISIONS.md D251: “every article of that day sees the same list”; D264: “questions open at the start of the item's day”.

problem: The conflict with the named views PRD is missing.
correct: Record that the PRD's general read rule does not describe the extraction snapshot.
evidence: docs/prd/06-views.md §Ordering: “An item reads only records from earlier sequences plus its own round's writes”; docs/DECISIONS.md D264 specifies the day-start extraction snapshot.

problem: The standing rule omits pull mode's exact tagged-value lookup.
correct: Include that pull mode looks up an exact tagged value when a condition needs one.
evidence: docs/DECISIONS.md D32: “pull mode looks up an exact tagged value when a condition needs one”.

problem: The quote joins two non-contiguous passages with a semicolon that is not in Alex's words.
correct: Quote the two passages separately, preserving their original text.
evidence: docs/DECISIONS.md D32 separates “如果是财报直接进来，那就不用重复XBRL了啊，这不是废话吗” from “keep the shape of the pipeline as is, don't 自己加戏”.

problem: The rule presents the modules' 2026-10-18 text as still frozen unchanged, although later decisions amended those modules.
correct: The modules were frozen as v1 in their 2026-10-18 text; subsequent changes require a new decision and have been made through later decisions.
evidence: docs/DECISIONS.md D37: “A change to a frozen module needs a new decision” and “Changed by D41: extraction, Config, the universe and the review pool were changed”.

problem: The ladder rule omits the decided two-rung case for a yes-or-no question.
correct: A yes-or-no question has two rungs; the other described ladders have five.
evidence: docs/DECISIONS.md D38, “Changed by D42: a yes-or-no question has two rungs”; D42, Ladders.

problem: The rule says one item is one judging round, but that was changed to one judging round per day.
correct: The day's items are written in sequence, then changed open views are judged in one daily round.
evidence: docs/DECISIONS.md D63: “Re-judging moves from each item's round to one round per day”.

problem: The named home still describes judging per item, but the conflict is absent.
correct: Record the conflict between D63's daily judging round and the views PRD's item intake step.
evidence: docs/prd/06-views.md §One item entering the library, step 7: “Run a rejudgement round”; docs/DECISIONS.md D63: “one round per day”.

problem: The detailed matching-record fields are presented as all standing, although D45 explicitly returned labelling details to proposal status.
correct: Distinguish the decided requirement to retain matching records, obtain human labels and later use a smaller model from the labelling details left as proposals, and identify the fields that later decisions actually retain.
evidence: docs/DECISIONS.md D40: “which records are sampled, the test set, measuring with labels, the training data and ‘no reinforcement learning’ are proposals”; D45 lists “the labelling details” as proposals.

problem: The rule says evidence without a link is not extracted, but the current one-decider path can extract it and then drop it for having no home.
correct: An extracted statement with no home is dropped from filing; do not say it cannot be extracted.
evidence: docs/DECISIONS.md D264: “one linked to nothing is dropped as 'no home'”.

problem: The rule requires every candidate to carry evidence, omitting the personal-memo exception.
correct: A candidate from the user's own memo may lack evidence.
evidence: docs/DECISIONS.md D59 changes D42 and D46 item 16: “a candidate carries evidence, except one read from Alex's own memo”; docs/prd/05-extraction.md §Two outputs gives the same exception.

problem: The later decision containing the personal-memo exception is missing.
correct: Add D59.
evidence: docs/DECISIONS.md D59: “Changes: D42 and D46 item 16 (a candidate carries evidence, except one read from Alex's own memo)”.

problem: The one-home wording leaves out the coverage-start exception.
correct: The daily path keeps the one-home rule; a coverage-start figure read by several questions is stored once and linked to each question that read it.
evidence: docs/DECISIONS.md D364: “存一条，挂到每道读到它的题” and “D207, D265 and D360 stand for the daily path”.

problem: The decision establishing the coverage-start exception is missing.
correct: Add D364.
evidence: docs/DECISIONS.md D364: “a figure several questions read is one record linked to each of them”.

problem: The quote joins two separate passages with a semicolon that is not in Alex's words.
correct: Quote the attachment and binary-ladder passages separately.
evidence: docs/DECISIONS.md D42 identifies them separately as “On attaching evidence” and “on two rungs”.

problem: The record marks disagreement because no governing document states the rule; absence alone is not a contradicting sentence.
correct: Do not mark the home as contradicting the rule without a contradictory passage; distinguish missing coverage from disagreement.
evidence: docs/DECISIONS.md D50: “D43's rule that a sealed copy is never edited stands”; the record supplies no contradicting sentence from docs/archive/.

problem: The record broadens D45's allowance for earlier decisions from decisions in force before the rebuild to any decision in force.
correct: D45's original scope was the views database and its extraction handoff, and it allowed a decision in force from before the rebuild as a source.
evidence: docs/DECISIONS.md D45: “in the views database and in what extraction hands to it” and “a decision in force from before the rebuild”.

problem: The rule retains judging once per item round after D63 changed judging to once per day.
correct: Judge changed open views in a daily round, dependencies first, each once.
evidence: docs/DECISIONS.md D63: “Re-judging moves from each item's round to one round per day”.

problem: D63, which changes the stated judging frequency, is missing.
correct: Add D63.
evidence: docs/DECISIONS.md D63: “one round per day”.

problem: The rule retains a separate model comparison call for candidate evidence as a current requirement, although matching now uses Jev by default.
correct: Candidate evidence is compared after its destination is resolved; identify Jev as the default matcher and the separate collision judge where applicable, rather than requiring the original general-model call.
evidence: docs/DECISIONS.md D47: “one more model call”; D190: “Jev answers every candidate-to-thesis relation and every evidence comparison since D169”.

problem: The later matching decisions are missing.
correct: Add D169 and D190 for the changed matching mechanism.
evidence: docs/DECISIONS.md D169 makes Jev the default matching engine; D190 retains Jev and adds the collision judge for specified candidate collisions.

problem: The named views PRD still describes the former additional model call, but the conflict is absent.
correct: Record that the PRD's step 4 describes a further comparison call while the current default uses Jev for evidence comparisons.
evidence: docs/prd/06-views.md §One item entering the library, step 4: “uses one further comparison call”; docs/DECISIONS.md D190: “Jev answers every candidate-to-thesis relation and every evidence comparison since D169”.
